stories.headline: NIA court frees 4 held for 2020 Srinagar terror attack that killed 2 soldiers
stories.title: NIA court frees 4 held for 2020 Srinagar terror attack that killed 2 soldiers
stories.summary: A special NIA court ruled that four men were not guilty of aiding terrorists in the 2020 attack. The prosecution could not establish any direct link between the men and the terrorists involved in the incident. Although two Army soldiers were killed, the evidence presented was circumstantial and insufficient. The court emphasized the necessity of legal proof despite the crime's severity and implications.

stories.headline: No Winter Session of Parliament? Skipped only four times in history
stories.title: No Winter Session of Parliament? Skipped only four times in history
stories.summary: Each previous instance coincided with extraordinary disruptions, from the Emergency and Lok Sabha dissolutions to Indira Gandhi’s assassination and the COVID-19 pandemic
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The Winter Session of Parliament has been skipped only four times in India’s parliamentary history, and each instance was linked to exceptional circumstances, including the Emergency, the premature dissolution of the Lok Sabha, the assassination of Prime Minister Indira Gandhi, and the COVID-19 pandemic.

With the Monsoon Session yet to be prorogued, setting a record for Parliament remaining unprorogued for more than 100 days, speculation has grown over the possibility of a short special session to consider the delimitation Bill.
The absence of any move to summon Parliament for its customary winter sitting has also fuelled discussion about whether the session could be skipped altogether.
The first time Parliament missed its winter session was during the 19-month Emergency.
The Lok Sabha met from July 21 to August 7, 1975, and then only from January 5 to February 6, 1976, without sitting during November or December, when the Winter Session is normally held.
The next instance came in 1979 after the premature dissolution of the Sixth Lok Sabha on August 22.
The newly elected House met only in January 1980, resulting in the Winter Session being skipped.
A similar situation arose in 1984 following the assassination of Prime Minister Indira Gandhi on October 31.
General elections were called, and the Eighth Lok Sabha held its first sitting on January 15, 1985.
After a gap of 36 years, the Winter Session was skipped again in 2020 during the COVID-19 pandemic.
Amid fears over the spread of the virus and stringent social-distancing norms, Parliament did not meet after the truncated Monsoon Session that ran from September 14 to 23.
In the 12 years of the Narendra Modi government, the timing of the Winter Session has varied considerably.

stories.headline: India announces Rs 15,000-crore assistance package for Nepal
stories.title: India announces Rs 15,000-crore assistance package for Nepal
stories.summary: New Delhi, Nov 23: New Delhi on Monday announced a development assistance package of Rs 15,000 crore for Nepal, including Rs 3,500 crore in grants for post-disaster reconstruction and infrastructure projects and a Rs 11,500-crore line of credit for energy sector projects. The announcement was made during talks between Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his Nepalese counterpart Balendra Shah, who was on his first State Visit to India since assuming office. The two Prime Ministers also adopted a Joint Vision for a “Viksit Bharat and Samunnat Nepal”, laying out an ambitious roadmap to strengthen bilateral cooperation in areas ranging from economic development, connectivity and energy to digital services, space, innovation and disaster management. PM Modi reaffirmed India’s unwavering support for Nepal’s development journey, describing the neighbouring country as a close friend. Nepal Prime Minister Shah, in turn, appreciated India’s humanitarian and technical assistance following the devastating Rasuwa-Bhotekoshi floods in Nepal. The assistance package includes Rs 3,500 crore in grant assistance (NPR 5,600 crore) and a rupee-denominated line of credit of Rs 11,500 crore (NPR 18,400 crore). Specific projects and modalities will be finalised through mutual consultations. Connectivity emerged as a major focus of the discussions, with PM Modi announcing a new transit trade route for Nepal through Deendayal Port at Kandla in Gujarat. Access to Paradip Port in Odisha will also be provided once the required infrastructure is in place. The two sides agreed to make the existing Kathmandu-Bhairahawa-Lucknow B345 air route bidirectional, with technical consultations to finalise the arrangements. The leaders also flagged off the inaugural Sarayu-Kamala Express rail service between Ayodhya and Janakpur, a move expected to boost religious and cultural tourism along the Ramayana Circuit and strengthen civilisational ties between the two countries. India and Nepal also finalised the Field Location Survey for the proposed Raxaul-Kathmandu electrified broad-gauge railway line. They agreed to collaborate in developing Nepal’s East-West Railway. The two Prime Ministers virtually laid the foundation stone for a new Integrated Check Post (ICP) at Banbasa and welcomed progress on similar facilities at Bhairahawa, Sunauli and Dodhara-Chandani. A new motorable bridge connecting Dharchula in India with Darchula in Nepal was also inaugurated to improve cross-border connectivity. In the energy sector, the leaders dedicated Phase II of the Motihari-Amlekhgunj petroleum pipeline to the people of Nepal and virtually laid the foundation stone for a petroleum terminal at Jhapa. They stressed the need for an early start to work on the Siliguri-Jhapa pipeline and agreed to explore cooperation in developing gas pipelines. The two sides also welcomed progress in hydropower cooperation and the participation of Indian companies in Nepal’s energy sector. The leaders virtually laid the foundation stone for the 669 MW Lower Arun Hydroelectric Project. They directed the Pancheshwar Development Authority and the Joint Committee on Water Resources to expedite the finalisation of the Detailed Project Report of the Pancheshwar Multipurpose Project and begin its implementation. Work on the DPRs of the Saptakoshi and Sunkoshi multipurpose projects will also be accelerated to utilise water resources and mitigate floods. The two countries also reviewed progress towards setting up joint ventures for two high-capacity cross-border transmission lines connecting Inaruwa-New Purnea and Dododhara-Bareilly. In the education sector, India agreed to establish an offshore IIT campus in Nepal to strengthen technical education and promote employment opportunities. The two leaders welcomed expanding cooperation in technology, start-ups and digital and financial connectivity. They also emphasised the need to facilitate easier access to banking and telecom services for citizens of one country living in the other. Eight memoranda of understanding were exchanged during the visit, covering cooperation in forensic sciences, police training, civil service capacity-building, traditional medicine, satellite communication, sustainable urban development, healthcare, and livestock and fisheries development. The two leaders also reviewed progress in ongoing development projects, including High Impact Community Development Projects and the construction of Nepal’s National Police Academy with Indian assistance. They welcomed the announcement of an Agro-Industrial Park in Chitwan, to be established with Indian grant assistance. On the boundary issue, the leaders noted progress in joint fieldwork for the maintenance and repair of boundary pillars and directed their Foreign Secretaries to work towards resolving outstanding boundary issues. Shah also called on President Droupadi Murmu and paid homage to Mahatma Gandhi at Rajghat. External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar called on the visiting Prime Minister. Shah thanked PM Modi for the hospitality extended to him and his delegation and invited him to visit Nepal. Modi accepted the invitation, with dates to be finalised through diplomatic channels.
